problem: Existing object-navigation methods and open-vocabulary scene graphs (ConceptGraph, HOV-SG, VLMap) handle only static, semantic-level targets. They cannot represent carrying relations between furniture and everyday items, nor update the map when items are moved, so navigating to a specific displaced instance (e.g. a red cup) is inefficient or fails.
motivation: Everyday items such as cups have unfixed positions, multiple same-category instances and changing carriers. A robot must therefore keep its scene representation up to date while it navigates. Since small items are usually carried by static furniture, the carrier layer gives a compact search space and an efficient update mechanism.
key_idea: Build an open-vocabulary Carrier-Relationship Scene Graph linking static carriers to the items they carry, update the carried sets online during navigation, and drive instance search as an MDP that combines feature similarity with LLM commonsense over carriers.
insight: Updating the CRSG during navigation raises SPL over successive targets, because observations made while finding the first object refresh the positions of the others, giving near point-to-point paths later; without updates SPL does not improve. In the single-object ablation, LLM-guided carrier selection (SPL 0.309) beats random carrier selection (0.205), and adding candidate-target prioritization reaches 0.342. Combining SBERT text similarity with GPT-4o image matching gives the highest SR overall in the long-sequence experiments.
method: Instance map with captions: builds an open-vocabulary 3D instance map from pre-collected RGB-D. Each object stores a CLIP feature, a caption list from Tokenize Anything and an SBERT text feature.
Building/Room layer: projects wall and door point clouds to the x-y plane and finds closed room contours by line search, assigning objects to rooms.

Carrier layer: selects objects whose SBERT similarity to 'furniture for holding objects' exceeds a threshold. GPT-4o filters them from the top-3 captions, then size and ground-contact criteria give the final carriers.
Object layer: assigns non-carrier objects to carriers via size, nearest distance and x-y-z overlap (function h), giving the carried set C(O_j).

MDP navigation policy: state (pose, unexplored carriers, candidate targets, found flag) with actions Stop / Explore(carrier) / Goto(candidate). Candidates are ranked by P_R = w1*ss*exp(-alpha*d~)/(1+w2*d). If there are no candidates, the LLM picks the most likely carrier to explore.
CRSG adaptation: matches new observations (CropFormer, TAP, CLIP, SBERT) to carrier objects by size, center distance and feature similarity. It then adds, removes or keeps carried objects.
Target verification: combines SBERT text similarity with a GPT-4o image comparison (for image goals) against a threshold sigma_2 to set the found flag.

results: Object query on an outdated offline map reaches 86% SR versus 62% for ConceptGraph and 44% for VLMap. In long-sequence navigation the full method generally achieves the highest SR and Tasks_SR versus text-only and LLM-only matching. SPL rises for later objects as the CRSG updates, and the method was also demonstrated on a real Autolabor robot.
limitations: Relies on an offline pre-built map; online mapping is left to future work
Small custom evaluation (3 Gibson scenes, few objects, no standard benchmark or strong navigation baselines such as GOAT)
Depends on GPT-4o and many foundation models, with high computation cost and no parallelism; real-world validation is a single qualitative example
